deck.title: CloudFront & Global Accelerator
deck.analogy: CloudFront is a bookstore chain stocking popular books in local stores (content closer); Global Accelerator is a private highway to the same warehouse (journey faster).

cards.front: What are the two opposite strategies AWS offers to fight distance latency (CloudFront vs Global Accelerator)?

back.answer: CloudFront brings the CONTENT closer (cache); Global Accelerator makes the JOURNEY faster (AWS backbone).
back.explanation: Content closer vs journey faster solves most exam questions.

cards.front: How many edge locations does CloudFront cache content at?

back.answer: 400+ edge locations worldwide.
back.explanation: First request is a cache miss; later requests are cache hits served from the edge.

cards.front: How does Global Accelerator speed up traffic without caching?

back.answer: User traffic enters the AWS private backbone at the nearest edge location and rides AWS fiber to the app.
back.explanation: It avoids the congested public internet; nothing is cached or copied.

cards.front: What can be a CloudFront origin?

back.answer: S3 buckets, ALBs, or any HTTP server — even outside AWS.
back.explanation: The origin is where CloudFront fetches the real content.

cards.front: What is CloudFront TTL and how does it affect origin load?

back.answer: How long an edge keeps a cached copy; longer TTL means fewer origin trips and less origin load.
back.explanation: "Reduce load on origin" = increase TTL / improve caching.

cards.front: What is a CloudFront invalidation and what is the cheaper habit?

back.answer: Force-expiring cached content early (e.g. /*); it costs money — use versioned filenames instead.

cards.front: Does CloudFront only help static content?

back.answer: No — CloudFront also accelerates DYNAMIC content via AWS's network from edge to origin.
back.explanation: Even uncacheable requests benefit; don't dismiss CloudFront because content isn't static.

cards.front: What does CloudFront OAC (Origin Access Control) do?

back.answer: Makes the S3 bucket private and grants only CloudFront the right to read it.
back.explanation: Prevents users from bypassing CloudFront's caching and paywall by hitting S3 directly.

cards.front: "S3 content must be accessible ONLY via CloudFront" — OAC or OAI?

back.answer: OAC. OAI (Origin Access Identity) is the legacy distractor.

cards.front: CloudFront Signed URL: what scope, and what's the signal?

back.answer: ONE file — "give a customer access to a single video/file".

cards.front: CloudFront Signed Cookies: what scope, and what's the signal?

back.answer: MANY files — "subscribers can access the whole premium library".

cards.front: What is CloudFront Geo Restriction?

back.answer: Allow-list or block-list entire countries at the edge.
back.explanation: Signals: "licensing agreements", "block users from country X".

cards.front: Which region must the ACM certificate be in for a custom SSL cert on CloudFront?

back.answer: us-east-1, no matter where anything else lives.
back.explanation: Free exam point.

cards.front: What is CloudFront field-level encryption?

back.answer: Encrypts specific sensitive form fields (e.g. credit card) at the edge so only the final application can decrypt.
back.explanation: Not even the origin infrastructure can read them.

cards.front: How many static IPs does Global Accelerator give you, and of what kind?

back.answer: 2 static anycast IP addresses that work worldwide and never change.
back.explanation: Anycast routes each user to the nearest AWS edge announcing those IPs.

cards.front: Why is Global Accelerator (not CloudFront) the whitelisting answer?

back.answer: GA has static IPs; CloudFront uses thousands of shifting edge IPs.
back.explanation: When client firewalls demand fixed IPs to allow, only GA helps.

cards.front: What protocols does Global Accelerator handle?

back.answer: ANY TCP or UDP traffic — not just HTTP.
back.explanation: Signals: gaming (UDP), VoIP, IoT, MQTT.

cards.front: Does Global Accelerator cache content?

back.answer: No caching, ever.
back.mnemonic: GA is a road, not a warehouse

cards.front: How fast is Global Accelerator failover and why is there no DNS lag?

back.answer: ~30 seconds; GA is in the request path and clients keep the same two IPs.
back.explanation: Solves Route 53 failover's weakness of clients caching old DNS answers.

cards.front: CloudFront vs Global Accelerator: strategy?

back.answer: CloudFront: content closer (cache). GA: journey faster (backbone).

cards.front: CloudFront vs Global Accelerator: protocol?

back.answer: CloudFront: HTTP/HTTPS. GA: any TCP/UDP.

cards.front: CloudFront vs Global Accelerator: caching?

back.answer: CloudFront: yes — that's the point. GA: no — never.

cards.front: CloudFront vs Global Accelerator: static IPs?

back.answer: CloudFront: no (many changing edge IPs). GA: yes — 2 static anycast IPs.

cards.front: CloudFront vs Global Accelerator: failover?

back.answer: CloudFront: n/a (origin failover exists). GA: in-path, ~30s, no DNS lag.

cards.front: CloudFront vs Global Accelerator: use cases?

back.answer: CloudFront: websites, video, APIs, downloads. GA: gaming, VoIP, IoT, whitelisting, instant multi-region failover.

cards.front: CloudFront vs S3 Transfer Acceleration vs Global Accelerator: how to pick by traffic direction/protocol?

back.answer: Download/view HTTP → CloudFront; upload to S3 → S3 Transfer Acceleration; TCP/UDP non-HTTP → Global Accelerator.
back.explanation: Read the direction and protocol of the traffic.
back.code:
Global users DOWNLOAD/view content (HTTP)   → CloudFront
Global users UPLOAD to an S3 bucket         → S3 Transfer Acceleration
Global users use a TCP/UDP app (non-HTTP)   → Global Accelerator

cards.front: What is S3 Transfer Acceleration for, compared to CloudFront?

back.answer: Uploads into S3 over the same edge network.
back.explanation: Exact signal: "users worldwide upload large files to a central bucket".

cards.front: What is a CloudFront origin group?

back.answer: Primary + secondary origin pair; on primary errors CloudFront automatically retries the secondary.
back.explanation: THE answer to CloudFront high availability / origin failover; geo restriction is the false twin.

cards.front: What does CloudFront price class control?

back.answer: Which edge locations the distribution uses — a cost dial (all = best latency, fewer = cheaper).
back.explanation: Nothing to do with routing to origins.

cards.front: Serve a static website worldwide with low latency; the S3 bucket must not be publicly accessible. Which CloudFront setup?

back.answer: CloudFront + S3 origin + OAC.
back.explanation: Cache at edges and lock the bucket to CloudFront only.

choices.why: Edge caching plus bucket locked to CloudFront.

choices.text: Global Accelerator in front of S3

cards.front: Paying subscribers should stream any video in the premium catalog via CloudFront. What do you use?

back.answer: Signed Cookies.
back.explanation: MANY files = cookies; ONE file = signed URL.

choices.why: Signed URL is for one file.
Encrypts form fields, not access control.

cards.front: Send a customer a CloudFront link to download a single report. What do you use?

back.answer: Signed URL.
back.explanation: One file, one URL.

choices.why: Locks bucket, doesn't grant per-user access.

cards.front: A multiplayer game over UDP has high latency for global players. Which service: CloudFront or Global Accelerator?

back.answer: Global Accelerator.
back.explanation: UDP rules out CloudFront instantly.

choices.why: Handles any TCP/UDP over AWS backbone.

cards.front: Enterprise clients' firewalls require a small set of FIXED IPs to whitelist. CloudFront or Global Accelerator?

back.answer: Global Accelerator.
back.explanation: 2 static anycast IPs — the only global service that offers this.

cards.front: A multi-region app needs failover in seconds without waiting for DNS caches. Which service: Global Accelerator, CloudFront, or Route 53?

back.answer: Global Accelerator.
back.explanation: In-path health checks, same IPs before and after.

cards.front: Licensing forbids streaming content in certain countries. Which CloudFront feature?

back.answer: CloudFront Geo Restriction.
back.explanation: Country-level block at the edge.

cards.front: Reduce the load on the origin server behind CloudFront. What do you do?

back.answer: Increase TTL / improve cache hit ratio.
back.explanation: More hits at the edge = fewer origin fetches.

choices.why: Increases origin fetches and costs money.

choices.text: Increase TTL / improve cache hit ratio
choices.why: More edge hits, fewer origin fetches.

cards.front: Users worldwide upload large files into one S3 bucket and uploads are slow. CloudFront, Global Accelerator, or S3 Transfer Acceleration?

back.answer: S3 Transfer Acceleration.
back.explanation: UPLOAD direction — not CloudFront.

choices.why: For TCP/UDP apps, not S3 uploads.
Edge network for uploads into S3.

cards.front: Attach a custom domain certificate to a CloudFront distribution whose app runs in eu-west-1. Where is the cert?

back.answer: ACM certificate in us-east-1.
back.explanation: Always, regardless of your app's region.

choices.text: IAM-stored cert in the app's region

cards.front: Keyword: **"global static content, low latency"**

back.answer: CloudFront

cards.front: Keyword: **"S3 only via CloudFront, private bucket"**

back.answer: OAC (OAI = legacy distractor)

cards.front: Keyword: **"one paid file"**

back.answer: Signed URL

cards.front: Keyword: **"whole paid library"**

back.answer: Signed Cookies

cards.front: Keyword: **"block/allow countries"**

back.answer: Geo Restriction

cards.front: Keyword: **"CloudFront custom cert"**

back.answer: ACM in us-east-1

cards.front: Keyword: **"encrypt one sensitive field end-to-end"**

back.answer: Field-level encryption

cards.front: Keyword: **"reduce origin load"**

back.answer: Longer TTL / better caching

cards.front: Keyword: **"force-refresh cached files"**

back.answer: Invalidation (/*, costs money)

cards.front: Keyword: **"UDP / gaming / VoIP / non-HTTP"**

back.answer: Global Accelerator

cards.front: Keyword: **"fixed IPs for whitelisting"**

back.answer: Global Accelerator (2 anycast IPs)

cards.front: Keyword: **"instant failover, no DNS-cache lag"**

back.answer: Global Accelerator

cards.front: Keyword: **"global UPLOADS to S3"**

back.answer: S3 Transfer Acceleration
